title.narrative: Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024
Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024

description.narrative:
The Ukuthula Trust seeks to achieve these broader objectives through the following objectives:
Project Goal: To deepen democracy by empowering people to release their energy towards taking an active part in the development and governance of their communities, through rehabilitation of communities and through prevention of conflict in Zimbabwe in the future by generating knowledge and promoting accountability.
1. Deepening Democracy: To empower and promote poor and marginalized communities, especially women and youth, in a bid to increase local and national government transparency, accountability and responsiveness to those communities 2. Restoring Social Fabric and Rehabilitating Victims of Collective Violence: To improve community cohesion, including women and youth, so that all community members can actively participate in the development of their community. 3. Generating Knowledge: To actively promote the re-examining of concepts linked to democracy, youth, gender, development and the histories of violence in Zimbabwe. 4. Lobbying and Advocacy: To promote and influence policy change in Zimbabwe.

Ukuthula Trust försöker uppnå dessa bredare mål genom följande:
Projektmål: Att fördjupa demokratin genom att ge människor möjlighet att aktivt ta del i utvecklingen och styrningen av sina samhällen, genom rehabilitering av samhällen, och genom att förebygga framtida konflikter i Zimbabwe genom att generera kunskap och främja ansvarsskyldighet. 1.Fördjupad demokrati: Att stärka och främja fattiga och marginaliserade samhällen, med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar, i ett försök att öka den lokala och nationella regeringens öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och lyhördhet för dessa samhällen.
2.Återställa social struktur och rehabilitera offer för kollektivt våld: Att förbättra samhällets sammanhållning, inklusive kvinnor och ungdomar, så att alla medlemmar i samhället aktivt kan delta i utvecklingen.
3.Skapa kunskap: Att aktivt främja omprövning av begrepp kopplade till demokrati, ungdom, kön, utveckling och historiskt våld i Zimbabwe.
4.Lobbying och påverkansarbete: Att främja och påverka politiska förändringar i Zimbabwe.

This COP presents preliminary results of the intervention and outlines the Embassy rationale and context for not renewing its agreement with Ukuthula. Final reports from Ukuthula, expected in August, will provide comprehensive results since the interventions inception and will be detailed in the completion memo.
As part of a strategic restructuring to realign development cooperation priorities, the Embassy reduced the number of partner organizations in its Human Rights, Democracy, Rule of Law, and Gender Equality portfolio. This led to the phasing out of several agreements, including the long-standing partnership with Ukuthula. To support a responsible exit, the Embassy provided additional funding to ensure a smooth conclusion of activities and proper documentation of results.
This transition took place in a challenging political environment, marked by a shrinking civic space and increased restrictions on civil society, human rights defenders, and citizens. Organizations operating in this space faced heightened scrutiny, limited freedom of expression, and constrained opportunities for public participation. Despite these difficult conditions, the Embassy remained committed to ensuring a responsible and impactful conclusion to its partnerships.
To that end, the Embassy extended support to Ukuthula for a final twelve-month activity period, from 1 March 2024 to 28 February 2025. An additional SEK 2,000,000 was allocated for this purpose, bringing the total phase-out funding to SEK 3,000,000. This final phase was designed not only to conclude the partnership but also to consolidate and sustain the gains made over the years.
During this period, Ukuthula concentrated its efforts on strengthening the sustainability of its interventions and empowering communities in rural Matabeleland North (Lupane) and Matabeleland South (Gwanda). The initiative aimed to mobilize community energy for local development and to restore the social fabric, enabling citizens to participate actively in decision-making processes and to demand accountability and transparency from their leaders even in an increasingly repressive environment.
Enhanced Community Engagement: Over 30 community forums were conducted, creating inclusive spaces for dialogue between citizens and local authorities. These forums helped rebuild trust and fostered a culture of open communication. As a result, communities began to engage more proactively in local governance, contributing to the development of community action plans and influencing local policy decisions.
Capacity Building: More than 500 community members received training in civic education, leadership, and participatory governance. This investment in human capital led to the emergence of local champions - individuals who have since taken on leadership roles in their communities. Many have become facilitators, peer educators, or members of local development committees, ensuring that civic engagement continues beyond the life of the project.
Improved Local Accountability: Community monitoring groups were established in both Lupane and Gwanda. These groups have played a critical role in tracking service delivery and holding local authorities accountable. Their presence has led to more timely responses to community concerns, greater transparency in resource allocation, and increased inclusion of marginalized voices in governance processes.
Content Development: Locally driven communication materials were produced to support civic education and raise awareness of rights. These included posters, radio messages, and community theater scripts tailored to local contexts. The materials have become valuable tools for ongoing education and advocacy, and are now being used by schools, community groups, and local NGOs to sustain awareness and engagement.
In parallel with its final implementation phase, Ukuthula placed strong emphasis on sustainability to ensure that the positive outcomes of its work would endure beyond the funding period. A comprehensive sustainability strategy was developed, focusing on four key areas:
1. Institutional Partnerships: Ukuthula established collaborations with local NGOs, traditional leadership structures, and government departments. These partnerships aimed to embed key activities such as civic education, community mobilization, and accountability mechanisms within existing community systems.
These partnerships are expected to increase the legitimacy and reach of Ukuthulas initiatives.They have the potential to influence policy by integrating successful practices into local governance frameworks.Local institutions are more likely to continue activities such as community forums and civic training, ensuring long-term impact.
2. Local Ownership: Community-based facilitators were trained to independently carry forward civic education and mobilization efforts. This approach fosters a sense of ownership and responsibility among community members.Embedded facilitators ensure that civic education remains a continuous, grassroots-driven process.Local facilitators are better positioned to adapt messages to the cultural and social context of their communities.
3. Resource Mobilization. Ukuthula initiated efforts to diversify its funding sources by submitting proposals to local philanthropic organizations and engaging private sector actors. These efforts enhance financial resilience by reducing reliance on a single donor. Diversified funding supports innovation and growth. Engaging local funders fosters a shared commitment to community development.
4. Knowledge Transfer: Ukuthula developed toolkits and training manuals, which were handed over to local partners to support the replication and scaling of successful approaches. This promotes scalability and ensures institutional memory. Local partners gain the skills and tools needed to implement and adapt interventions independently. Knowledge transfer strengthens community capacity and supports long-term sustainability.
The phase-out period officially concluded in February 2025. At present, the Embassy is awaiting the submission of final reports from Ukuthula. These reports will inform the completion memo, in which all key results, lessons learned, and strategic insights will be articulated in detail.
